architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Let Delta_pct be the measured 120-130 C viscosity-level change relative to the matched unmodified E2 reactive-core reference. Accept exactly one registered hypothesis if Delta_pct is within plus or minus 3.40 percentage points of its prediction: H-LEVEL-DILUTE at -42.76%, H-LEVEL-ASSOC at 17.24%, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC at -72.76%. This is a formulation-level classification only, not evidence of a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The processing-window viscosity level is measured directly in the selected resin-modified chemistry, so it does not depend on transfer of the unmodified-family thermal shape. The E_eta descriptor is also measured from this candidate sweep, although it is fit-derived. Thus the primary level observable remains inside direct chemistry support, while no unmodified-family regularity is assumed for reconstruction.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if Delta_pct differs from -42.76% by more than 3.40 percentage points. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if Delta_pct is at or below -42.76%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if Delta_pct is at or above -42.76%. A result outside all three acceptance bands falsifies all three registered level rules for this realized composition, but does not distinguish modifier-axis effects or interaction from preparation-state variability.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-REPEAT with at least three independent S1C41 preparations and matched unmodified E2 reference sweeps, then establish the discrimination threshold from the replicate uncertainty before re-adjudicating the level hypotheses.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level at 120 and 130 C, with the viscosity curve across 80-130 C; E_eta from the ln(eta) versus 1/T fit is secondary.
judge_normalized.rationale: The binding chemistry audit excludes M-ANCHOR for modified chemistry but explicitly permits M-SWEEP as direct shape verification. This experiment directly measures the unresolved processing-window viscosity level and provides the strongest available separation of the three registered formulation-level predictions. The choice is therefore a discriminating probe, with formal numeric criteria retained but interpreted cautiously because realization-state uncertainty is substantially larger than the nominal threshold.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-SWEEP because it is an admissible direct measurement, lies in the deterministic top tie, and uses the smallest sufficient dual-axis intervention. I followed the Skeptic in restricting interpretation: the one-preparation protocol cannot reliably establish a 3.40 percentage-point modifier effect against the observed realization spread, and the dual-axis result cannot support separate acrylic, tackifier, or interaction attribution.

uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the primary 120-130 C level because it is directly measured; higher for any interpretation based on E_eta or comparison with the unmodified shared shape.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The M-SWEEP discrimination resolution is 3.40 percentage points based on the supplied sweep residual; direct 120-130 C readings are preferable to shape reconstruction.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High relative to the registered 3.40 percentage-point threshold because the selected card specifies one preparation and the supplied E2 data show CV 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original reactive polyurethane reactive-core family represented by E1–E3, with the E1 +P chemical perturbation treated separately. An experiment introducing acrylic-like or tackifier-like modifiers would change chemistry and would not automatically remain inside the validated support of the shared local thermal shape; direct temperature-sweep verification is therefore required unless the chemistry audit establishes support.
planner.failure_mode: The modified candidate may miss the processing-viscosity window at 120–130 °C because its realized viscosity level is not established and may be displaced by modifier-specific effects or realization variability.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The measured E2 temperature sweeps fall from a mean of 18,530.7 at 80 °C to 3,322.0 at 130 °C, while nominal run spread remains large, with CV 0.464–0.585 and max/min ratios 2.80–3.57; no modified-candidate viscosity level has been directly measured.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local data resolve viscosity levels for original unmodified formulations across temperature, but do not directly resolve the level of a modified candidate relative to its inert-dilution baseline. The large E2 run spread further limits discrimination of modifier effects unless the candidate is measured directly.
measurement_requirements: Measure the candidate directly by an 80–130 °C viscosity sweep in 10 °C increments on a freshly prepared sample, including direct measurements at 120 and 130 °C.
Use a matched unmodified reactive-core reference and compare the candidate level with the declared inert-dilution prediction at the same temperatures.
Collect sufficient repeat measurements to distinguish elevation above dilution from depression below dilution beyond the stated measurement resolution.
Record the apparent temperature-response descriptor from ln(eta) versus 1/T rather than assuming transfer of the local shared shape.
planner.scientific_question: At matched temperature and reactive-core composition, does the modifier change the realized viscosity level according to inert dilution, raise it above dilution as predicted by acrylic association, or depress it below dilution as predicted by plasticization?

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: This is needed to recover the evidence-derived candidate-space axes, reactive-core anchor, and historical claim boundary before comparing candidate experiment cards.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The candidate is resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry, outside the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was previously measured. The primary processing-window level is nevertheless measured directly by M-SWEEP rather than reconstructed from the shared shape, so the experiment is admissible as direct chemistry-specific shape verification. The fitted E_eta descriptor remains model-derived, but the level observable at the decision temperatures is direct.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If the measured 120-130 C level change relative to the matched unmodified reactive core falls within 3.40% of exactly one prediction (-42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC), that hypothesis is accepted for S1C41 and the directly measured processing-window viscosity level is reported with it.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change departs from -42.76% by more than 3.40%. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured change is at or below -42.76%, and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above -42.76%. Thus, a result on the depression side falsifies association, a result on the elevation side falsifies plasticization, and a sufficiently displaced result falsifies inert dilution.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result not within 3.40% of any registered prediction would support none of the three pre-registered level rules and would indicate an unregistered modifier interaction, process-state effect, or inadequate resolution. The direct sweep would still establish the candidate-specific processing-window level and its observed thermal response, but no registered level hypothesis would be accepted.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C, including the realized level at 120 and 130 C, together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses a higher 17.5% acrylic loading and therefore a larger departure from the characterized reactive chemistry without adding hypothesis discrimination.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses a higher 20% acrylic loading and a larger intervention burden than necessary for the same direct discrimination.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses a 22.5% acrylic loading, increasing modifier burden without improving the measurement plan or registered-hypothesis separation.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses the largest 25% acrylic loading in the tied set, making it the least conservative intervention despite identical information value.

proposer.reasoning: The planner identifies realized viscosity level as the least-resolved coordinate and requires direct measurement across the processing window. M-SWEEP directly measures that quantity, verifies the thermal response in the chemistry-shifted candidate, and separates all three registered level hypotheses at the stated 3.40% resolution. S1C41 remains inside the externally supported dual-axis intervention region and is the least burdensome member of the deterministic top tie.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI component vectors and are scientifically tied by the deterministic layer. S1C41 is selected because it uses the smallest acrylic loading in the tied set while retaining the independently supported 5% minor-tackifier level, which lies in the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster. It therefore provides the smallest sufficient dual-axis perturbation within the supported conservative acrylic region while retaining full discrimination of all three level hypotheses.

residual_decision_risk: One planned preparation cannot distinguish a 3.40% modifier effect from preparation-state variability.
The protocol does not explicitly include a matched unmodified reactive-core reference under the same sweep protocol.
The dual-axis result cannot separately attribute a level change to AC1920, TK100, or their interaction.
The apparent E_eta descriptor remains fit-derived, even though the 120-130 C level is directly measured.
The chemistry applicability audit is binding: shared-shape reconstruction via M-ANCHOR is inadmissible for this modified chemistry; the sweep verifies rather than assumes the thermal response.
The five-way deterministic tie is not resolved by VOI; S1C41 is retained because it is the least burdensome tied intervention within the supported region.
Decision stability describes stability of the transparent score, not confidence, posterior probability, or correctness of the experiment.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is that the declared 3.40% discrimination threshold is not attainable with one preparation when the supplied E2 data show much larger preparation-to-preparation variability. This does not make another selectable card a better answer to the primary processing-window level question: M-SWEEP still directly measures the candidate at 120-130 C, whereas M-REPEAT does not return that level. The result should therefore be interpreted as a direct candidate-level and curve observation unless independent preparations, a matched unmodified reference, and a replicate-based uncertainty threshold are added. The registered hypothesis acceptances and mechanistic attribution should not be treated as established at the stated 3.40% threshold. The dual-axis formulation also leaves acrylic, tackifier, and interaction effects entangled; this limits attribution rather than changing the direct level measurement to run.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: S1C41::M-SWEEP remains in the tied top experiment set under every reported weight perturbation. The top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, the top_experiment_set_mean_jaccard is 1.0, and recommendation_flip_boundary reports no flips for any weight term across the full 0.5x-1.5x sweep. These perturbations are scientifically defensible because they vary budget efficiency, decision relevance, extrapolation risk, hypothesis discrimination, measurement interpretability, process-state risk, and uncertainty reduction without changing the direct-measurement requirement. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.002292.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary 120-130 C viscosity level is inside direct measurement support because S1C41 uses M-SWEEP across 80-130 C. The prior shared thermal-response shape is outside its measured chemistry support and is appropriately used only for verification, not reconstruction. The E_eta descriptor remains fit-derived and chemistry-specific only insofar as the candidate sweep verifies it.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The stated 3.40% criterion is based on a fitted-sweep residual, not on the between-preparation variability of the proposed candidate protocol. With one repeat and process_state_risk scored 0.75, the protocol cannot demonstrate that a deviation of 3.40% is reproducible or modifier-caused. Multiple independent preparations, a matched unmodified reference measured under the same protocol, and a predeclared replicate-based uncertainty threshold are required.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could support only a composition-level deviation from the registered level rules, not the claimed acrylic-association or two-axis plasticization attribution.
objections.objection: For S1C41, the registered prediction separations are mathematically larger than the stated 3.40% M-SWEEP threshold: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is -42.76%, H-LEVEL-ASSOC is 17.24%, and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is -72.76%. However, the experiment changes both acrylic_like to 15% and minor_tackifier_like to 5%. Thus it cannot identify whether an elevation or depression is caused by the acrylic-like axis, the tackifier-like axis, or their interaction. The proposer declares hypotheses_not_separated as an empty list and therefore does not admit this attribution entanglement.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any acceptance of H-LEVEL-ASSOC would over-attribute a dual-axis composition result to acrylic chemistry, and any rejection of H-LEVEL-PLASTIC would not establish that the acrylic axis is non-plasticizing.
objections.objection: The formulation_state for S1C41 simultaneously replaces 20% of the E2 reactive core with AC1920 at 15% and TK100 at 5%. H-LEVEL-ASSOC depends only on acrylic_like, whereas H-LEVEL-PLASTIC depends on the total of both axes. With no single-axis control or factorial comparison, the primary level change cannot distinguish acrylic association from a TK100 contribution or an AC1920-TK100 interaction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The processing-window level itself remains interpretable, but the quantitative comparison to -42.76%, 17.24%, and -72.76% could inherit reference-state or normalization assumptions not covered by the stated protocol.
objections.objection: The 120-130 C level is directly measured by M-SWEEP, which is a strength. But the reported E_eta descriptor is obtained by regressing ln(eta) against 1/T, and the acceptance comparison still requires computing a relative level change against a matched unmodified reactive-core reference. The M-SWEEP protocol specifies only the candidate sweep and does not explicitly include measurement of that matched reference under the same run protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Treating the E_eta fit as prior-supported without the direct sweep would overstate chemistry-domain evidence, but the proposed direct sweep itself avoids that error.
objections.objection: The candidate is resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 and the shared thermal shape was measured only in unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry. The proposal correctly uses M-SWEEP with shared_shape_use set to verification_only rather than M-ANCHOR, so the primary 120-130 C level stays inside direct measurement support. The fitted E_eta descriptor remains model-derived, but this does not undermine the directly measured level observable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result can be labeled as falsifying H-LEVEL-DILUTE, H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC when the observed difference is actually preparation-state variability rather than a modifier effect.
objections.objection: The falsification threshold for S1C41 is 3.40%, based on the M-SWEEP multiplicative RMSE of 1.034x. The protocol requires only min_repeats: 1 and does not control realization state, while the audit reports E2 nominal run spread of CV 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57. That observed preparation variability is vastly larger than 3.40%, so a single fresh-sample sweep cannot reliably determine whether the candidate differs from the inert-dilution prediction by more than the declared threshold.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A rheological level shift would be incorrectly reported as proof of molecular association, plasticization, or a specific modifier interaction.
objections.objection: The experiment measures viscosity level and a rheological E_eta descriptor, but it cannot establish the molecular mechanisms named in the hypothesis statements, such as acrylic association or plasticizing-continuum behavior. The payload's claim boundary correctly says the registered hypotheses are formulation-level statements and make no molecular-mechanism claim; the proposer should therefore not interpret acceptance as mechanistic confirmation.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run multiple independent preparations of S1C41 and the matched unmodified E2 reactive-core reference under the same 80-130 C sweep protocol, then set the discrimination threshold from the replicate uncertainty rather than the 3.40% fitted RMSE. If axis attribution is required, add single-axis controls at matched AC1920 and TK100 loadings or use a factorial design; otherwise restrict the conclusion to a composition-level result.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 3.40% falsification threshold is not attainable with min_repeats: 1 and no realization-state control when the supplied E2 data show CV 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57. The experiment may directly measure the candidate curve, but it cannot reliably discriminate the registered level predictions at the declared resolution.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.admissibility_reason: The 80-130 C sweep is the direct verification measurement that establishes the thermal-response shape for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

budget_efficiency_detail.definition: 1 - effort_points / max(effort_points) over the declared catalog

top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured level change is at or below the inert-dilution prediction of -42.76%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above that same prediction. H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change departs from -42.76% by more than the 3.40% resolution of this plan.

measurement_plan.name: 80-130 C temperature sweep
measurement_plan.primary_observable: directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T
measurement_plan.protocol: Measure viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample and regress ln(eta) against 1/T.
